thread:
evan: Quick ask — ran a lightweight onboarding smoke for ember-11b on canary. Publishing numbers here and asking for a quick sanity check before we push to the main catalog. TL;DR: 8 tokens/sec p50 on p4d-ish profile, weird mem spike at step ~12. Full log below.

sara: thanks — can you paste the run command and env?

evan: run command: ```./bench_run --model ember-11b --seq 512 --bs 1 --profile --device p4d --quant none --kv-cache on``` env: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0, runtime=v2.3.1

sara: pasted quick summary from the profiler: 
- steady throughput: ~7.8-8.2 tok/s (seq512, bs1)
- p50 latency: 1250ms, p90: 1900ms, p99: 4200ms
- peak GPU mem: 47.3GB (device had 48GB)
- observed a 0.6s stall at step 12, then mem usage jumped ~1.8GB for 2 steps then returned

kai: that mem jump sounds like intermittent KV cache growth or allocator fragmentation. Did you see any OOMs?

evan: no OOMs, just that temporary increase. I captured a short snippet of the logs: 
```
[12:34:56] step=11 tokens=1024 rt=1.18s
[12:34:57] step=12 tokens=1536 rt=2.01s WARN: large alloc(1811934208)
[12:34:59] step=13 tokens=2048 rt=1.20s
```

maggie: hmm - WARN: large alloc indicates a transient buffer. Could be attention tiling fallback or backend trying a different kernel. Can you re-run with `--dump-allocs` and `--kernel-trace`? That should show which op caused the alloc. Also try `--kv-cache off` to see if it disappears.

eran (ops-bot): deploy/canary ember-11b @canary-cluster started by evan at 2026-03-16T12:03:21Z :rocket:

ryan: cost question — what's the tokens/sec delta vs ember-7b? If ember-11b is 2.5x slower but improves quality, we might want a smaller batch/pinning strategy.

sara: quick compare (same seq/bs): ember-7b p50=480ms p90=900ms p99=1700ms, tok/s ~20. So ember-11b is ~2.5x slower indeed.

kai: actionable checklist: 
1) evan: re-run with `--dump-allocs --kernel-trace` and `--kv-cache off` (low effort)
2) sara: collect full perf counters + nvprof snapshot if possible
3) maggie: recommend quantization profile candidates after we see traces
4) ryan: prepare cost/quality trade doc for product before catalog publish

evan: on it. I'll run the two quick variations and post traces here by EOD. If we can't repro the alloc after kv-cache off, maybe it's just a pathological prompt for our test vector.

maggie: small note — if kernel trace shows attention fallback, try `--tile-size 64` to avoid fallback on long sequences. Also add `--max-seq 1024` to ensure allocator prefetch is exercised.

ryan: sounds good. If you need GPU time I can open a priority slot for an hour. :thumbsup:

evan: grabbing the slot now. will post results (trace + condensed numbers) in this thread. thanks everyone.

ops-bot: canary/deploy ember-11b completed smoke run (no OOM) — logs archived: http://ci.internal/logs/ember-11b/canary/3191234567

sara: thanks — once evan posts traces I'll do a short regression check against our standard prompt set and callout any quality regressions.

evan: posted follow-ups in thread (traces + small CSV) — marking this as in-progress.
